version.changelog: Release 1.0.3: the Windows app is now a separate download (ModelBox on GitHub Releases) instead of a bundled binary.

llm.summary: The kit’s purpose is coherent, but its setup guidance misleadingly dismisses script risks while recommending removal of Windows download protections.

dimensions.detail: Default writes are proportionate to a local setup kit. A user-selected -Workspace path can be outside the profile, contradicting the absolute profile-only claim; this is explicitly configurable rather than hidden access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The FAQ claims Defender has nothing to block because there is no binary, while the install guide unblocks every bundled PowerShell and Python script. Directions to read scripts first mitigate this, but the guidance still misrepresents script safety and does not explain the protection being removed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Setup is user-invoked, skill installation has an explicit skip option, and workflow execution requires a menu selection or command argument.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent changes are the disclosed workspace, installed skills, and Start Menu shortcut. No service, scheduled task, automatic startup, or elevation request appears in the bundled code.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Creating a workspace, installing three named workflow skills, and offering a launcher fit the stated purpose. The bundled code shows no credential harvesting, trading, email sending, or telemetry.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review downloaded scripts and their source before unblocking individual files, and investigate security warnings instead of relying on the FAQ’s reassurance. Review the three separately installed skills before launching them. The optional unsigned ModelBox application is outside this package’s code review; its supplied checksum does not establish safety.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The advisory concern is not supported as a material authority problem: environment use serves ordinary path discovery and disclosed optional provider configuration. Missing tool declarations alone do not establish excessive permissions.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Artifact review supports concern about the misleading safety assurance accompanying blanket unblocking, although reviewed scripts may legitimately need unblocking. Microsoft confirms that this removes the Internet-origin marker and permits unsigned downloaded scripts under RemoteSigned. [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/unblock-file)
[SDI-4] expected: Downgraded to a documentation inconsistency: the install guide explicitly demonstrates a custom workspace outside the profile, and the code writes to that user-selected location without gaining additional privileges.
